subject: Data path bordering and temporary hop request
messages:
From: Elena Park <dpo@acmehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Liu <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data path bordering — temporary hop request and telemetry scope

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Before legal signs the DPA addendum, our security team asked for two clarifications so we can close procurement:

1) Temporary-hop window: we need a written commitment that any cross-region "temporary hop" for failover or scaling will be limited to a maximum of 72 hours and that we will be notified within 1 hour of any such event with start/end timestamps.

2) Telemetry & replication visibility: we require that any telemetry or replication involving Acme Health data be logged to our audit trail (read-accessible) and that logs indicate the destination region, kernel/instance id (or opaque route id), and whether KMS keys were customer-managed for the hop.

We attached a redlined DPA addendum with small language edits and a request to list Redwood subprocessors that might be involved in cross-region routing. Can you confirm whether you can provide the subprocessor roster and the timeline for when the roster will be updated in your portal?

Tom is on copy for procurement cadence. We need these clarified to finish our internal sign-off by next week.

Regards,
Elena Park
Data Protection Officer
Acme Health

Attachment: DPA_Addendum_ACME_redlined.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <dpo@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data path bordering — temporary hop request and telemetry scope

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the redlines. We're aligned on the goal: minimize exposure while keeping predictable availability. A few notes and next steps below; I'll loop in Ops and Legal for exact language.

Short answers up front:
- Temporary-hop window: we can commit to a default 48-hour automatic window for transient failover/replication with an option to extend to 72 hours only with explicit customer approval (we can surface an email-level approval flow).
- Notification SLA: we will commit to an internal 1-hour alert and a customer-visible notification within 1 hour of the start of any hop.
- Telemetry: we can provide immutable audit logs showing timestamp, source region, destination region, route id, and KMS key id. For KMS: by default we use Redwood-managed keys; customer-managed keys (BYOK) are supported and will be indicated in the logs.

Requested from you: can you confirm whether a 48-hour default + opt-in 72-hour extension is acceptable? If so, we'll draft precise DPA language and populate the subprocessor roster export.

Jonas/Karthik — can you confirm the ops/logging attachments I asked for below and whether we can include a stub subprocessor roster (CSV) for Acme to review?

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Security & Compliance (Sales-eng alignment)
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data path bordering — temporary hop request and telemetry scope

Stephanie / team — technical ops details below; copying in the items I'll attach for Acme.

1) Temporary-hop mechanics:
- We coordinate failover via our smart routing layer. A "temporary hop" occurs when sessions or KV cache shards are replicated to a different region to maintain latency or throughput. We can restrict this to the minimal shard set required and cap automatic duration to 48 hours. Extensions to 72 hours require an approval ticket (email or signed DocuSign).

2) Notification & audit trail: 
- We log: event_id, timestamp_utc, source_region, dest_region, route_id, instance_id (opaque), action (replicate/failover), reason_code.
- KMS metadata: key_id and key_owner_type (redwood/customer).
- Logs are exportable as newline-delimited JSON; we'll provide an export sample.

3) Subprocessors: current roster attached (subprocessor_roster_2027-03.csv). The roster includes roles (edge cache, analytics, monitoring), their country, and contact point. Note: some edge cache providers may appear as transient endpoints but don't receive plaintext customer data; we mark their processing type in the roster.

Attachments included: subprocessor_roster_2027-03.csv (CSV, 9KB), transient_hop_log_sample.ndjson (NDJSON sample, 7KB).

Operational constraints / suggestions for DPA wording (draft language we recommend):
- "Redwood will restrict automatic cross-region replication for Acme Health customer data to 48 hours unless written authorization for an extension to 72 hours is provided."
- "Redwood will notify Acme Health within one (1) hour of any automatic cross-region replication start; notification will include start time, expected end time, affected resource ids, and destination region."

I kept the wording conservative; legal can tighten.

Jonas Weber
Head of Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: subprocessor_roster_2027-03.csv
Attachment: transient_hop_log_sample.ndjson

Elena / Tom — thanks for the patience. From a procurement/contracting perspective:

- If Acme accepts the 48-hour default with an opt-in 72-hour extension, we can push the DPA addendum through DocuSign today and target signature within 48 hours. I've attached a DocuSign link with the redlined version Stephanie referenced.
- Pricing/credits: because this is an operational constraint that can impact capacity planning we can include a one-time on-boarding credit to cover telemetry ingestion and audit exports. We can confirm the amount once legal signs off on exact wording.
- Subprocessor transparency: the roster Jonas attached is the current live export; we will commit to updating the roster in our portal within 5 business days of any change and notifying Acme by email for any new subprocessors that could materially access or route customer data.

DocuSign: https://docusign.net/ACME-DPA-2027
